A subcontractor who justifiably stops work after the other party's material breach may elect restitution for the reasonable value of the performance conferred, less payments received, without deduction for the loss it would have suffered by completing and without the contract price as a ceiling.

A party is estopped from asserting the statute of frauds where refusing enforcement would cause unconscionable injury to one who seriously changed position in reliance on the oral agreement, or would unjustly enrich one who accepted its benefits; no representation about a writing is required.

Under Connecticut's one-year statute of frauds provision, an oral contract that does not expressly prescribe a duration beyond one year is treated as of indefinite duration and falls outside the provision, however long performance will actually take.

A grantee who accepts a deed is bound by its mortgage-assumption clause even without signing it, and that promise to the grantor is an original undertaking, not a promise to answer for another's debt within the suretyship statute of frauds.

A contract is voidable when mental illness or defect makes a person unable to act reasonably in relation to the transaction and the other party has reason to know of the condition, even if the person understood the transaction.

A minor who disaffirms a fair purchase made without overreaching, after paying money and using the article, may recover the price only subject to the seller's reasonable compensation for use, depreciation, and willful or negligent damage.

An enforceable arbitration agreement requires a writing, an unambiguous intent to submit to arbitration, and bilateral consideration; a handbook arbitration clause acknowledged only as non-contractual information, and changeable by the employer at any time without notice, lacks assent and consideration.

A ward under a valid adjudication-based guardianship cannot incur contractual duties, and the guardianship order gives constructive public notice of incapacity, so a seller without actual knowledge can neither enforce the contract nor claim restitution.

Undue influence is excessive persuasion that overcomes a person's will by exploiting weakness or distress; it needs neither misrepresentation nor a confidential relationship, and consent so obtained may be rescinded.

A contract modification is voidable for economic duress when a party threatens to withhold goods owed under a contract, and the threatened party cannot obtain them from another source in time and an ordinary action for breach would be inadequate.

A contract freely made at arm's length without fraud is not void as against public policy merely because one party's return is large or the goods will ultimately be sold to the government; public policy must rest on identifiable law and precedent.

A seller who has performed does not ordinarily lose the right to payment merely because the buyer plans an improper use of the goods, but a seller who acts to further that improper use may be denied enforcement on public-policy grounds.

Under Illinois common law, in-house counsel generally cannot bring a retaliatory-discharge tort claim against the employer-client, because the public policy at stake is protected by the lawyer's mandatory professional duties.

A trivial and innocent departure from a construction contract does not forfeit the builder's right to the price but is compensated in damages, measured by diminution in value when the cost of replacement is grossly and unfairly disproportionate to the benefit.

When one party unequivocally renounces a contract before performance is due, the other may treat it as breached, consider himself released from future performance, and sue immediately for damages, or may instead await the performance date.

A buyer's competing purchases that merely make the seller's performance more difficult and expensive do not excuse the seller's breach; prevention excuses performance only where, as with an agreed exclusive source, the other party's conduct actually prevents it.

Anticipatory repudiation requires an absolute and unequivocal refusal to perform or a distinct and positive statement of inability; describing difficulty in obtaining materials and asking for help is not a repudiation.

A clause requiring consent to assignment limits the right but not the power to assign; an unauthorized assignment is effective, though a breach, unless the agreement clearly manifests that a nonconforming assignment is void or ineffective.

Under UCC § 9-404(a)(1), an assignee's rights are subject to all terms of the agreement between the account debtor and the assignor and to defenses arising from that transaction, regardless of when the account debtor received notice of the assignment.

A completed sale of a specific article cannot be undone at law for mistake where both parties were ignorant of its true nature and value and the article delivered was the article sold; absent fraud, inadequacy of price alone gives no right to recover it.

A party's apparent assent may be avoided, before or after completion, when the bargain rests on a mutual mistake of material fact going to the substance of the thing bargained for, but not when the mistake concerns only its quality or an accidental attribute.

A buyer who keeps goods beyond a reasonable time without rejecting them cannot afterward rescind the sale for an innocent misrepresentation about a quality such as authorship; any remaining remedy is damages.

Rescission for mutual mistake requires a mistaken belief about an existing fact that relates to a basic assumption and materially affects the agreed performances, and it is unavailable to a party who bears the risk of the mistake, as under an acceptance-of-present-condition clause.

Notice must be reasonably calculated under the circumstances to reach the person affected; posting an eviction notice on a tenant's door is inadequate where posted notices are known to be frequently removed and feasible measures such as mail could improve reliability.

When a mortgagee is reasonably identifiable from a publicly recorded mortgage, due process requires that publication of a tax sale be supplemented by notice mailed to its last known available address or by personal service.

A forum may bind absent plaintiff-class members on money claims without minimum contacts if they receive the best practicable notice, a chance to be heard, a chance to opt out, and adequate representation; but it may apply its own law only to claims with sufficient forum contacts.

When a probate nonclaim period is triggered by court-ordered proceedings and extinguishes a creditor's claim, due process requires notice by mail or a comparably reliable means to creditors who are known or reasonably ascertainable; publication suffices only for the rest.

The adequacy of notice is judged under Mullane's standard of notice reasonably calculated under the circumstances, which requires a reasonable effort to inform the interested person rather than proof of actual receipt.
When a mailed notice of a tax sale is returned unclaimed before the sale, due process requires the state to take additional reasonable steps to notify the owner if it is practicable to do so.

A party cannot secure personal service on an otherwise out-of-reach nonresident by fraud, trickery, artifice or a wrongful device, used by the party or someone acting for the party, that induces the person to enter the court's territorial jurisdiction; such service will be set aside.

Contracting parties may agree in advance to submit to a court's jurisdiction, and a person a contract designates to receive process is an agent authorized by appointment under the Federal Rule when she promptly accepts and transmits the process, even without an express promise to do so.

Service on a corporation is valid when delivered to an employee so integrated with the organization that he will know what to do with the papers, even without express authorization; losing the papers internally afterward is not excusable neglect.

The Hague Service Convention applies only when the forum's internal law requires documents to be transmitted abroad to complete service; where valid service on a foreign corporation is complete domestically, the Convention does not apply.
A person may have more than one dwelling or usual place of abode for service of process, provided each has sufficient signs of permanence; actual notice does not cure service that is otherwise void.

A default judgment entered without valid service is void for lack of personal jurisdiction and must be vacated; actual receipt of the papers cannot by itself cure delivery to someone who is not the defendant's officer or authorized agent.

Under § 1608(a)(3) of the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, a service packet for a foreign state must be mailed directly to the foreign minister at the minister's office in the foreign state, not to the state's embassy in the United States.

Rule 35 permits a mental or physical examination of any party, defendant as well as plaintiff, but only on an affirmative showing that each condition is genuinely in controversy and that there is good cause for each particular examination.

The party resisting discovery bears the burden of justifying its refusal, and labelling an interrogatory a contention interrogatory does not make it premature; a party must answer with the facts it presently has and may amend or supplement later.

Under Rule 26(b)(1) discovery must be relevant and proportional to the needs of the case, and in a products-liability case discovery of other designs is measured on a sliding scale of similarity to the product at issue.

A court may allow discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference on good cause, meaning the discovery is needed for the suit to progress, if the plaintiff has a good-faith basis for personal jurisdiction, and may attach conditions protecting the person to be identified.

Witness statements, memoranda and mental impressions that a lawyer prepares in anticipation of litigation, though outside attorney-client privilege, cannot be obtained in discovery as of right; the party seeking them must show adequate reasons, such as necessity, for the intrusion.

Corporate attorney-client privilege is not limited to a control group: it protects confidential communications from employees to counsel, made at management's direction about matters within their duties, to obtain legal advice; work product revealing counsel's mental processes needs more than substantial need and undue hardship.

Rule 16(f) and a court's local rules authorize sanctions, including fines payable to the court and imposed on the party itself, for failing to prepare for and participate in good faith in court-ordered mediation, even where the party relied on its counsel.

The Seventh Amendment jury right extends to those issues in a shareholder derivative suit on which the corporation would have been entitled to a jury had it sued directly.

The trial judge may permit jurors to submit witness questions while screening out irrelevant or argumentative questions. This concerns trial administration, not the existence of a jury right.

When the Government seeks civil penalties on a statutory claim that is legal in nature, such as securities fraud closely related to common-law fraud, the Seventh Amendment requires a jury trial in an Article III court unless the public-rights exception applies.

Under the Seventh Amendment's Reexamination Clause as read in 1913, an appellate court that finds the evidence insufficient may not enter judgment against an unconditional general jury verdict but must order a new trial.

The Seventh Amendment permits judgment for a defendant after a plaintiff's jury verdict when the trial judge expressly reserved the defendant's sufficiency motions and took the verdict subject to their resolution.

Directing a verdict when the claimant's proof leaves an essential fact to speculation rather than reasonable inference does not violate the Seventh Amendment, which preserves the fundamental jury institution rather than every procedural detail.

A plaintiff must prove by a preponderance both negligence and its proximate contribution to the injury; a jury verdict cannot stand where the evidence leaves causation to speculation among possible explanations.

A prima facie case combined with sufficient evidence that the employer's stated justification is false may permit, but does not compel, an inference of intentional discrimination; under Rule 50 the court reviews the whole record without weighing evidence or resolving credibility.
